Du teilst Best Practices im Unternehmen und stärkst eine&nbsp;datengetriebene Entscheidungs- und Flow-Kultur.</p> <p><strong>Repräsentation<br></strong>Du vertrittst den Bereich Supply Chain &amp; Flow in Managementrunden, gegenüber Lieferanten und in funktionsübergreifenden Gremien</p> <h3><strong><br>Über dich</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Abgeschlossenes Studium im Bereich Logistik, Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen, Supply Chain Management oder einem vergleichbaren technischen oder wirtschaftlichen Fachgebiet.</li> <li>Mindestens 10 Jahre Erfahrung im Supply Chain Management, davon mehrere Jahre in einer takt- und flussorientierten Organisation (Bau, Modulbau, Holzbau, Fertigung, Werft, Maschinenbau).</li> <li>Nachweisliche Führungserfahrung in dynamischen, komplexen und stark wachsenden Umfeldern.</li> <li>Tiefes Verständnis von Materialfluss, Produktionslogistik, Taktplanung, Engpassmanagement (TOC), Transportlogistik und digitaler Supply-Chain-Steuerung.</li> <li>Erfahrung im Arbeiten mit ERP/APS-Systemen), Track-&amp;-Trace, ETA-Tools und KPI‑gesteuerten Control Tower Setups.</li> <li>Starke Kommunikations- und Moderationsfähigkeit über alle Ebenen hinweg.</li> <li>Verhandlungssichere Deutschkenntnisse, sehr gute Englischkenntnisse.</li> <li>Leidenschaft für industrialisiertes Bauen, datengetriebene Flow-Steuerung und die Weiterentwicklung skalierbarer Bauprozesse.</li> </ul> <h3><br>&nbsp;Was wir bieten</h3> <ul> <li>Ein unbefristeter Vertrag mit 30 Urlaubstagen.</li> <li>Flexible Arbeitsweise: Wir legen großen Wert auf regelmäßige persönliche Zusammenarbeit im Büro, und bieten auch die Möglichkeit zum Arbeiten im Homeoffice sowie die Option, bis zu 40 Tage im Jahr aus dem Ausland zu arbeiten.</li> <li>Attraktive Zusatzleistungen: Wir bieten eine betriebliche Altersvorsorge, Sprachkurse (Englisch/Deutsch) und Mitarbeiterrabatte bei ausgewählten nachhaltigen Marken. Darüber hinaus unterstützen Dich unsere externen Partner im Bereich mentale Gesundheit, um Deine psychische Gesundheit durch anonyme Einzel- oder Gruppensitzungen zu stärken.</li> <li>Virtuelles Aktienprogramm: Profitiere von GROPYUS Erfolg durch unser Virtuelles Aktienprogramm.</li> <li>Eigenverantwortung: Du kannst wirklich etwas bewirken – auf allen Ebenen unserer Organisation. Finde Lösungen, treibe sie voran, teste und implementiere sie.</li> <li>Die Chance, Teil von etwas Großem zu sein: Unsere Mission ist es, eine ganze Branche neu zu denken. Hilf uns dabei, das Bauwesen neu zu erfinden und nachhaltiges, erschwingliches Wohnen zu fördern.</li> <li>Ein vielfältiges und bereicherndes Arbeitsumfeld: Werde ein geschätztes Mitglied eines wunderbar vielfältigen Teams von Menschen aus über 50 Ländern. So werden unsere Unterschiede zu Stärken, die uns als Team weiterbringen.&nbsp;</li> </ul> </div><div class="content-conclusion"><h4>Join us on our mission to design buildings as continuously evolving products to create the most exciting and affordable experience for all. description: Bei uns übernimmst Du die fachliche Verantwortung beim Aufbau und der Weiterentwicklung unserer IT-Security und Infrastruktur. Durch unser Wachstum und steigende Security-Anforderungen bauen wir diesen Bereich gezielt weiter aus und suchen dafür einen erfahrenen Security-Experten. Dabei arbeitest Du eng mit unserem bestehenden IT-Team zusammen und übernimmst die Verantwortung für Security-Themen. Du bekommst den Freiraum, technische Entscheidungen zu treffen, Security-Standards zu etablieren und unsere IT-Landschaft nachhaltig mitzugestalten. Aufgaben Definition von Security-Standards: Du entwickelst konkrete und verbindliche Vorgaben und Regeln für die sichere Gestaltung und den sicheren Betrieb der IT. IT-Infrastruktur & Monitoring : Du analysierst und optimierst unsere Linux- und Windows-Infrastruktur und steuerst das Monitoring von Verfügbarkeit, Leistung, Kapazitäten und Zuständen unserer Systeme. System Hardening & Vulnerability Management: Du erarbeitest sichere Konfigurationen für unsere Server, Clients und Betriebssysteme, um Schwachstellen vorzubeugen. Außerdem werden vorhandene oder neue Schwachstellen von Dir erkannt, behoben und dokumentiert. Security Monitoring & SIEM: Du entwickelst das zentrale Logging, Monitoring und die Detection unserer Systeme weiter, bindest relevante Logquellen an das SIEM an und erstellst geeignete Erkennungs- und Alarmierungsregeln. Sicherheitsrelevante Ereignisse bewertest Du und leitest erforderliche Maßnahmen ein. Security-Bewertungen & technische Freigaben: Du prüfst neue Systeme auf Sicherheitsrisiken, leitest konkrete Anforderungen ab und triffst nachvollziehbare Freigabeentscheidungen. ISO 27001 & ISMS: Du wirkst maßgeblich am Aufbau unseres Informationssicherheitsmanagementsystems und an der Vorbereitung der ISO-27001-Zertifizierung mit. Dein Schwerpunkt liegt auf der Überführung regulatorischer und organisatorischer Anforderungen in wirksame technische Maßnahmen. Security by Design: Du begleitest Kundenprojekte und unterstützt die beteiligten Teams bei der Entwicklung sicherer Architekturen und Lösungen. Security Awareness: Du konzipierst und etablierst zielgruppengerechte Schulungen, Awareness-Kampagnen und praxisnahe Trainings und stärkst damit nachhaltig das Sicherheitsbewusstsein im Unternehmen. Unterstützung des IT-Betriebs: Du unterstützt das Team bei betrieblichen Aufgaben und Störungen und trägst zu einer zuverlässigen Bereitstellung unserer IT-Services bei. Qualifikation Du hast eine abgeschlossene IT-Ausbildung oder ein Studium im IT-Umfeld. Du bringst mindestens fünf Jahre relevante Berufserfahrung als IT-Security Engineer, Cyber Security Engineer, Cyber Security Architect, Systemadministrator, Informationssicherheitsbeauftragter (ISB), IT-Infrastructure Engineer, Consultant ISMS oder in einer ähnlichen Position mit. Du verfügst über fundierte Kenntnisse in den Bereichen IT-Security, Netzwerke, VPN, Firewalls sowie Linux- und Windows-Infrastrukturen. Idealerweise hast Du bereits praktisch am Aufbau eines ISMS bzw. an einer ISO-27001-Zertifizierung mitgewirkt. Kenntnisse in den Bereichen Penetration Testing, AWS, Azure, VMware, Proxmox, Microsoft 365 und Jira sind ein Plus. Du kommunizierst sehr gut auf Deutsch und Englisch – sowohl im technischen Umfeld als auch mit Kunden und anderen Fachbereichen. Du arbeitest eigenständig und strukturiert, analysierst Probleme gründlich und findest pragmatische Lösungen. Du treibst Themen selbstständig voran. Du bist bereit, Entscheidungen zu treffen, Verantwortung dafür zu übernehmen und Deine technische Einschätzung zu vertreten. Benefits Echter technischer Gestaltungsspielraum: Wir geben Dir nicht den Lösungsweg vor. Deine Erfahrung und Deine Ideen fließen in Entscheidungen ein. Anforderungen, die interessant bleiben: Neue Herausforderungen und anspruchsvolle Problemstellungen sorgen für technische Abwechslung und bieten Raum, Neues auszuprobieren. Zusammenarbeit auf Augenhöhe: Du arbeitest eigenverantwortlich und triffst auf Kolleg:innen, mit denen Du technische Ansätze diskutieren, hinterfragen und gemeinsam weiterdenken kannst. Flexibilität im Arbeitsalltag: Flexible Arbeitszeiten, ein Überstundenkonto und die Möglichkeit, gelegentlich im Home-Office zu arbeiten, geben Dir Spielraum bei der Gestaltung Deines Arbeitstags. Verbesserungen ausdrücklich erwünscht : Du siehst Potenzial in unseren Prozessen oder unserer Infrastruktur? Bring Dich ein. Technische Verbesserungen sollen bei uns nicht nur angesprochen, sondern auch umgesetzt werden. Sicherheit und langfristige Perspektive: Dich erwarten ein unbefristeter Arbeitsvertrag, eine private Unfallversicherung sowie die Möglichkeit zur betrieblichen Altersvorsorge. Benefits darüber hinaus: Hansefit, die Möglichkeit zum Business-Bike- oder E-Auto-Leasing, Corporate Benefits und weitere Angebote. Find more English Speaking Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

Wir sind eine der am schnellstwachsenden Digitalagenturen Hamburgs und suchen zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt neue Mitarbeiter/innen mit Schwerpunkt Wirtschaftsinformatik für den Bereich Business Development

Was macht die Cordes Consulting GmbH genau?

Wir sind eine Werbeagentur, welche Handwerksunternehmen durch innovative Social-Media-Strategien dabei hilft, mehr Bewerbungen von Fachkräften aus der Region zu erhalten. Wir vermarkten also mittelständische Unternehmen als attraktive Arbeitgeber in den sozialen Netzwerken.

Du hast Erfahrung mit digitalen Themen und kennst dich mit Low-Code-/No-Code-Lösungen sowie API-Tools wie Zapier oder Make.com aus – oder bist in der Lage, dich schnell und eigenständig einzuarbeiten? Dann ist unser Bereich IT und Business Development die richtige Abteilung für dich.

Als Fachinformatiker/-in gestaltest und automatisierst du unsere Prozesse mit modernen Tools. Du sorgst dafür, dass Systeme ineinandergreifen, Datenflüsse reibungslos funktionieren und unsere Abläufe noch effizienter werden.

Aufgabengebiete:

  • Automatisierung unserer Geschäftsprozesse mit No-Code / Low-Code Tools wie n8n, Zapier, Make

  • Aufbau, Pflege und Verwaltung von Airtable-Datenbanken

  • Entwicklung von Front-Ends und Interfaces mit No-Code / Low-Code-Tools

  • Management und Weiterentwicklung unseres CRM-Systems (insbesondere HubSpot)

  • Planung, Umsetzung und Implementierung von neuen Geschäftsprozessen

  • Dokumentation & Konzeption von digitalen Geschäftsprozessen

  • Anwenderschulung & -betreuung

Wenn du weitere Informationen zu unserem Unternehmen und deiner Karriere bei Cordes Consulting haben möchtest, findest du diese auf www.cordes-karriere.de.

Gehalt: Junior Fachinformatiker (m/w/d): 5.000 € brutto im Monat

Weiterentwicklungs- und Aufstiegsmöglichkeiten sind vorhanden.

Das erwartet Dich bei uns: 

  • Eine gute Vergütung über dem Branchendurchschnitt.

  • Ausführliche interne Schulung: Durch unser internes Schulungssystem lernst du alles, was du für deine neue Tätigkeit bei uns im Unternehmen benötigst.

  • Hervorragende Aufstiegsmöglichkeiten: Über die nächsten Jahre werden wir weiter stark wachsen.

  • Einen tollen Firmenstandort in der Hamburger Innenstadt

  • Eine tolle Arbeitsatmosphäre: Uns ist ein positives Umfeld wichtig. Der Umgang untereinander ist sehr kollegial und familiär. Wir ziehen alle am gleichen Strang.

  • Ein dynamisches Team und ein motivierendes Arbeitsumfeld.

  • Einen sicheren Arbeitsplatz: Jede Person, die wir einstellen, soll langfristig mit uns wachsen. Das Ziel jeder Einstellung ist eine unbefristete Übernahme.

  • Eine erstklassige Büroausstattung: Wir arbeiten ausschließlich mit moderner Technik und Arbeitsausstattung.

  • Wir übernehmen die Kosten für dein Deutschlandticket oder einen Tiefgaragenstellplatz in unserem Bürogebäude.

  • Cordes Consulting Gesundheitssystem: Profitiere von umfangreichen Gesundheitsleistungen für dich und deine Familienangehörigen (u. a. 900 € jährliches Gesundheitsbudget für Privatleistungen, Facharzt-Terminvereinbarung innerhalb von 5-10 Tagen, ärztliche Zweitmeinung sowie ein 24/7 Gesundheitstelefon)


  • Erfolgreich abgeschlossene Ausbildung als Fachinformatiker/-in (z. B. Fachrichtung Anwendungsentwicklung, Systemintegration, Digitale Vernetzung oder Daten- und Prozessanalyse) oder eine vergleichbare IT-Ausbildung, alternativ erste praktische Erfahrungen im Bereich IT / Automatisierung

  • Analytisch-methodisches und strukturiertes Denken, sehr gute analytische Fähigkeiten und schnelle Auffassungsgabe

  • Erste Erfahrungen im Projektmanagement sowie hohe Disziplin und Organisationsfähigkeit

  • Ergebnis- und lösungsorientierte Arbeitsweise, Fähigkeit bestehenden Prozessen zu folgen, diese zu verstehen und zu verbessern

  • Ausgeprägte Teamfähigkeit, starkes Kommunikationsvermögen und sicheres Auftreten

  • Sehr gute schriftliche Ausdrucksweise in Deutsch

  • Belastbarkeit und ein guter Umgang mit Leistungsdruck

Dann ist diese Stelle genau die richtige für dich! – Für uns sind deine persönliche Einstellung und dein Wille wichtiger als dein Lebenslauf! Our core mission is to deliver fully operational unmanned systems, integrating the critical subsystems, including Electronic Warfare, necessary for NATO forces to maintain a decisive advantage in contested environments. We do whatever is required to achieve platform autonomy, grounded in precision, responsibility, and uncompromising engineering discipline.


About the team

We are a lean, agile group with a strong systems-minded focus. We operate without silos, looking for proactive engineers who are excited to take mathematical models off the whiteboard and deploy them onto physical hardware. On our Electronic Warfare algorithms team, you will bridge the gap between theoretical signal processing and real-world hardware execution, taking direct ownership of key software and firmware modules.


Your mission

At STARK, we are building the next generation of autonomous platforms capable of navigating the world's most contested environments. As a Senior Mesh Network and MAC Engineer you will solve the critical challenges of directional wireless communication in highly dynamic networks. You will design and implement the medium access control (MAC) and routing layers that allow our platforms to form robust, self-healing networks under demanding tactical conditions.


Responsibilities

  • Architect and implement MAC protocols and routing algorithms tailored for directional multi-node systems, directly tackling the challenge of neighbour discovery under highly focused, narrow beams.
  • Build dynamic TDMA schedules and beam coordination mechanisms in lockstep with the physical layer (PHY) and antenna steering systems, ensuring routing decisions are grounded in real-time RF characteristics rather than simple hop counts.
  • Deliver resilient multi-hop relay capabilities that sustain high-bandwidth video and control links between mobile platforms over tactical distances, routing back seamlessly to ground control stations under dynamic conditions.
  • Build and maintain multi-node Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) testbeds alongside automated logging pipelines to quantitatively evaluate and verify network join times and topology reform behaviours.
  • Mesh networking in a product that shipped — sim work alone does not qualify — plus Linux networking at kernel and packet level with live debugging.
  • Radio-literate and has designed a medium-access scheme or TDMA schedule.


Qualifications

  • Deep, practical familiarity with the Linux networking stack at the kernel and packet levels, coupled with strong live-debugging skills on embedded systems.
  • Strong understanding of wireless propagation and physical layer realities, with hands-on experience designing medium-access control schemes or TDMA schedulers.


Nice to have

  • Active contributions to open-source routing protocols (e.g., batman-adv, olsrd, Babel).

You will be working closely with the Flight Test Team and reporting to the Technical Director.


Your mission

As a Flight Test Engineer & Onsite Test Coordinator, you are the "Conductor of the Flight Line." Depending on your seniority, you will be responsible for the end-to-end lifecycle of our flight test campaigns, from initial planning and hazard assessment to execution and deep-dive data analysis.
Beyond the technical data, you serve as the primary Onsite Leader. You are the person who ensures testing priorities are crystal clear to everyone on the range. You manage the daily tempo, coordinate the crew, and ensure that every person, from pilots to software engineers, knows exactly which tests are being conducted and when. Your mission is to transform raw flight data into actionable insights while maintaining a high-tempo, disciplined, and safe testing environment.




Responsibilities

Onsite Test Coordination & Leadership

  • Act as the Onsite Test Coordinator: Lead daily operations on the range, ensuring the team stays focused on the primary test objectives.
  • Clarify Priorities: Maintain and communicate the "Daily Flight Schedule," ensuring everyone knows the sequence of events and current testing priorities.
  • Lead Briefings: Drive the morning "Pre-Flight Brief" and the evening "Debrief," capturing critical feedback and setting goals for the following day.
  • Resource Management: Coordinate the availability of airframes, ground support equipment, and personnel to maximize range time efficiency.
Flight Execution & Safety
  • Coordinate and execute UAV flight tests in compliance with regulatory requirements and STARK safety standards.
  • Ensure all flight activities and anomalies are documented with high fidelity.
  • Develop specific Flight Test Techniques (FTTs) and instrumentation requirements to capture critical performance metrics.
  • Lead Flight Readiness Reviews (FRR) and contribute to safety review boards.
Test Design & Data Analysis
  • Develop comprehensive flight test plans, test cards, and rigorous flight test hazard assessments (FTHA).
  • Process and analyze flight data using MATLAB or Python to validate system performance against requirements.
  • Work closely with Ardupilot and PX4-based flight control systems to iterate on flight behavior and performance.
  • Manage the configuration of flight test articles, ensuring all hardware and software versions are meticulously tracked.


Qualifications

Educational & Legal Background

  • Degree: Bachelor’s or higher in Aerospace, Electrical, Mechanical, or Systems Engineering.
  • NATO Citizenship: Must be a citizen of a NATO member state (due to export control and security regulations).
  • Communication: Professional-level written and verbal English.
Technical & Leadership Toolkit
  • Coordination Skills: Proven ability to lead a technical team on-site (three pilots and one engineer), manage schedules, and communicate priorities clearly under pressure.
  • Data Mastery: Practical experience in data reduction and analysis using MATLAB or Python.
  • UAV Systems: Familiarity with Ground Control Stations (GCS), telemetry systems, and mission planning tools.
  • Testing Rigor: Proven ability to plan and conduct system-level tests in an aerospace or defense environment.
Mindset & Style
  • The "General" Mindset: You are naturally organized and can work through ambiguity on the flight line.
  • Analytical & Decisive: You can analyze a data anomaly quickly and decide whether to continue testing.
  • Meticulous Documenter: You believe that if it wasn't documented with high fidelity, the test never happened.
Preferred Experience
  • Active experience with uncrewed aviation.
  • Hands-on experience with flight test instrumentation (FTI) and DAQ systems.
  • Experience with Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) simulation environments.

We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.<br><br>Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.</p></div><p><strong>JOB DESCRIPTION</strong></p> <p><strong>Senior Manager, International Indirect Tax</strong></p> <ul> <li>Location: Mon remotely, Tue-Fri in-office (London, Amsterdam, Frankfurt, or Madrid)</li> <li>Reporting to: VP, Tax</li> <li>Reports: no formal direct reports, with broad influence on the global tax organization</li> </ul> <p>At Axon, we are on a mission to Protect Life. We build and deploy technology across public safety and justice, and we hold ourselves to high standards in how we operate — including in how we manage our obligations as a global business.</p> <p><strong>Your Impact</strong></p> <p>Axon is seeking a Senior Manager, International Indirect Tax to lead the company's international VAT and indirect tax function, encompassing all non-US VAT and indirect taxes. The role carries overall responsibility for the quality and accuracy of all indirect tax compliance output, as well as providing advisory support to internal teams on indirect tax matters arising from contracts, new market entry, entity set-up, and tax law changes.</p> <p>The successful candidate will be commercially minded, technically strong across European and global VAT systems, experienced in indirect tax compliance, and confident advising Finance, Legal, and Commercial colleagues without requiring escalation. The role supervises three indirect tax team members, reporting directly to the Vice President, Tax.&nbsp; Experience in a hardware and software business with a complex supply chain is highly desired.</p> <p><strong>What You’ll Do</strong></p> <p><strong>Internal Advisory</strong></p> <ul> <li>Act as the primary point of contact for non-US indirect tax queries across Finance, Legal, and Commercial teams.</li> <li>Liaise with sales teams and other partners to understand upstream sales processes that impact indirect tax operationalization and compliance matters.</li> <li>Advise on the VAT treatment of customer contracts, pricing structures, and invoicing arrangements, working directly with Sales and Legal as required.</li> <li>Provide VAT guidance on new product lines and SKU launches, including taxability assessments and sales tax code assignments in D365.</li> <li>Represent the indirect tax function in e-invoicing projects and regulatory change programmes.</li> <li>Support the business through tax authority audits, enquiries, and disputes.</li> <li>Monitor legislative developments across relevant jurisdictions and communicate implications to the business.</li> <li>Advise and inform management on growing areas of focus in non-US indirect compliance and audits, technology trends and solutions, and process improvements.&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>Compliance Oversight</strong></p> <ul> <li>Review and approve all indirect tax compliance deliverables — VAT returns, Intrastat, OSS, and ESL — across all in-scope jurisdictions, with full accountability for accuracy and submission deadlines.</li> <li>Oversee indirect tax accounting, including journal entries, balance sheet reconciliations, and BlackLine certification.</li> <li>Maintain the compliance calendar and validate data quality across all submissions.</li> <li>Monitor VAT payments and refunds; liaise with local tax authorities where required.</li> <li>Provide guidance to Finance and operational teams on compliance requirements as they arise.</li> </ul> <p><strong>New Entity Set-Up</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead the indirect tax workstream for all new entity formations, covering VAT registration, system readiness, and the preparation of compliant workpaper frameworks prior to first filing.</li> <li>Review and approve invoice templates for new entities before they commence trading.</li> <li>Ensure SOX and internal control obligations are met across all indirect tax processes.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Process and Systems</strong></p> <ul> <li>Identify and implement improvements to VAT filing workflows, including the use of AI, macros, Alteryx, and D365 configuration.</li> <li>Participate in or lead system testing for indirect tax-related ERP and reporting changes.</li> <li>Maintain commodity code tax tables and item sales tax code frameworks in D365.</li> <li>Ensure processes are documented and structured to support an expanding compliance footprint.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What You Bring</strong></p> <ul> <li>A minimum of 10 years' experience in VAT or indirect tax, gained in-house at a multinational or in a professional services environment.</li> <li>Detailed working knowledge of VAT across multiple European jurisdictions, including Intrastat, OSS, and ESL reporting obligations.</li> <li>Demonstrable experience reviewing and approving compliance deliverables prepared by others, with personal accountability for quality and timeliness.</li> <li>Experience advising on the indirect tax treatment of commercial contracts, pricing arrangements, and customer invoicing.</li> <li>Experience managing the indirect tax aspects of new entity set-ups, including VAT registration and process build-out.</li> <li>Familiarity with Microsoft D365 or a comparable ERP; working knowledge of BlackLine, Sigma, and Alteryx is advantageous.</li> <li>Understanding of SOX internal control requirements in a tax context.</li> <li>Ability to communicate clearly on technical VAT matters to non-specialist colleagues across Legal, Finance, and Commercial functions.</li> <li>Experience managing and leading a team.</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p>Don’t meet every single requirement? You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.</p> <p><strong>Important Notes</strong></p> <p><em>The above job description is not intended as, nor should it be construed as, exhaustive of all duties, responsibilities, skills, efforts, or working conditions associated with this job. title: Senior Product Designer - CRO, London, UK
description: <div class="content-intro"><h3>About Eucalyptus</h3> <p>We're on a mission to make good health last a lifetime. More than 1 billion people live with obesity worldwide, driving preventable chronic conditions. We're here to build better long-term care.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p>Eucalyptus is now part of Hims &amp; Hers, the global leader in personalised health and wellness.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p>Euc is the company behind Juniper, one of the world's largest weight-management programs combining GLP-1 medication with personalised nutrition, movement support, and clinician-led care from prescribers, nurses, health coaches, pharmacists, and dietitians. Our published clinical research shows that our combined clinical and behavioural approach helps patients lose significantly more weight during their treatment with Juniper by four times.<br><br></p> <h3>Our Growth Story:</h3> <ul> <li>Supporting patients living with obesity across our 5 markets</li> <li>Received selective NICE endorsement to provide services to the NHS</li> <li>Tailored our offering to thousands of patients in Australia, the UK, Germany, Japan and Canada.</li> </ul></div><p>People arrive at our pages ready to change their health, and unsure whether to begin. Starting a treatment that could change your life is a big decision, and often a frightening one. Your job is to help them take the first step.</p> <p>This is a Senior Product Designer role for someone who can make that moment clear, credible and human. You design the surfaces where people decide to start, some of the highest-stakes creative work we have, and you can measure your impact in the number of people who begin.</p> <p><strong><span class="notion-enable-hover" data-token-index="0">In this role, you will:</span></strong></p> <ul> <li>Design every page as an argument. Every element earns its place: the problem, the solution, the proof, the process, the value, and the blockers you remove.</li> <li>Own our highest-leverage acquisition surfaces end to end: landing pages, the signature conversion components on them, and the templates they sit in.</li> <li>Own the conversion-bearing pieces others don't, e.g. BMI calculators and the interstitial moments that carry someone through a clinical quiz and consult form, the points where people hesitate and leave.</li> <li>Make the case on every surface. Meet someone where they are in their decision and build a clear, structured argument for why to start, built around them, not a list of features.</li> <li>Translate clinical language into words a patient understands and trusts. Accurate, compliant and human at once.</li> <li>Design dense information like an infographic: communicate a lot, simply. Data visualisation and strong hierarchy in place of walls of text, without losing the detail. Our patients care about the detail, so your job is to convey it clearly, not to oversimplify.</li> <li>Lean on interaction design to carry the detail. Progressive disclosure, reveals and interactive data let people go as deep as they want, without meeting it all at once.</li> <li>Use motion and pacing with intent. You control the rhythm of a page and the beat between steps, so people keep moving.</li> <li>Carry the creative set from our adverts through to the landing page and the touchpoints after it. One unbroken story from ad to conversion.</li> <li>Partner your CRO manager on the optimisation loop. You bring the hypothesis and the design, shape the tests and read what comes back, and turn the result into the next move.</li> <li>Help more people start. That is the number you move, and you always know why it moved.</li> <li>Earn trust with evidence: multiple, specific proof points, not a logo and a star rating, all holding up in a regulated market.</li> </ul> <p><strong><span class="notion-enable-hover" data-token-index="0">What good looks like</span></strong></p> <ul> <li><strong><span class="notion-enable-hover" data-token-index="0">Scope:</span></strong> you own the front door. The acquisition surfaces where people decide whether to begin, and the design-led testing that keeps them improving.</li> <li><strong><span class="notion-enable-hover" data-token-index="0">Impact:</span></strong> you help more people get started. At our scale that reaches into millions of lives, real people beginning a treatment that changes theirs. You move that number, and you can show the before and after.</li> <li><strong><span class="notion-enable-hover" data-token-index="0">Influence:</span></strong> you work alongside growth experts, CROs, and product and commercial partners. You hold the bar on what is right for the patient, balancing it against the needs of the business. You bring people with you by offering options and choices, gaining buy-in with evidence rather than force. And you raise the bar inside the design team too, giving sharp critique and making the designers around you better.</li> </ul> <p><strong><span class="notion-enable-hover" data-token-index="0">About you (who you are)</span></strong></p> <p>The best person for this role has a rare mix. You make dense, complex medical information simple and clear, without dumbing it down or losing what matters. You are doing this for people at a vulnerable moment, so empathy and emotional intelligence are critical. You read the emotion in a health decision and meet people where they are, with warmth and without judgement. And you are deeply curious about health. You do not need to arrive knowing the conditions we treat, only the drive to understand them. You pair all of that with sharp acquisition craft and the discipline to test. You hold the human and the commercial in the same hand.</p> <p><strong><span class="notion-enable-hover" data-token-index="0">Skills &amp; experience</span></strong></p> <ul> <li><strong><span class="notion-enable-hover" data-token-index="0">Problem definition.</span></strong> You shape the problem, not just the pixels. You use data and research to work out which surface matters most and which experiment is worth running, then package it into something the team can build. The signal is evidence you helped define the right test, not just made the variant.</li> <li><strong><span class="notion-enable-hover" data-token-index="0">Visual craft.</span></strong> Non-negotiable. Typography, spacing, colour, motion and micro-interactions, used with intent, not decoration. This role also carries the interstitial illustration in the quiz and consult flow, so you make that visual work yourself. Weak craft is a no, whatever the conversion talk.</li> <li><strong><span class="notion-enable-hover" data-token-index="0">Accessibility.</span> </strong>You design inclusively without being asked. You know why the standard exists, not just what it says, and it shows in judgement calls a checklist cannot make.</li> <li><strong><span class="notion-enable-hover" data-token-index="0">Systems thinking.</span></strong> You think in modules, not single pages. You compose from the design system's primitives, own the signature, conversion-bearing components built on top, and build page templates that assemble in different ways to serve different needs. Modularity is your default and it keeps you fast, but you build bespoke, ground-up pages when a high-profile moment deserves the craft. You extend the system rather than reinvent it, and you keep a clean line between the atomic layer the system owns and the bespoke pieces you own. Infrastructure compounds. Single screens do not.</li> <li><strong><span class="notion-enable-hover" data-token-index="0">Product and commercial sense.</span></strong> You reason in conversion rate, cost per acquisition and funnel drop-off. You know which page matters most to the business and why, and you defend a design decision in the language of the metric it moves. Craft in isolation moves nothing.</li> <li><strong><span class="notion-enable-hover" data-token-index="0">Communication.</span> </strong>Clear, specific, opinionated. You say what you decided and why, and you are just as clear on what you chose not to do and why.</li> <li><strong><span class="notion-enable-hover" data-token-index="0">Working in the open.</span></strong> You share early and often, and you use critique to sharpen the work. You lift the quality of every review you join.</li> </ul> <p><strong><span class="notion-enable-hover" data-token-index="0">How you work with AI</span></strong></p> <ul> <li>LLMs are already embedded in your workflow. You use them to widen the range of variants you can test and to tighten the build-measure-learn loop.</li> <li>You prototype in tools like Claude Code and Cursor to test ideas in real code, not just mock them up.</li> <li>The signal is workflow, not tool count. Judgement spent where it counts.</li> </ul> <p><strong><span class="notion-enable-hover" data-token-index="0">The full stack</span></strong></p> <ul> <li>We expect you to work end to end, from problem definition and research to information architecture and UX writing.</li> <li>Validation and experimentation is the core of the role. You design A/B tests, size them, and read them honestly.</li> <li>Your own research and usability testing, feeding the next experiment.</li> <li>Copywriting and UX writing. You write the words that persuade and the words that guide, and both hold up in a regulated market.</li> <li>Composition from the design system, and ownership of the signature components and templates built on top of it.</li> </ul> <p><strong><span class="notion-enable-hover" data-token-index="0">Your portfolio</span></strong></p> <p>Show us work where you took something complex and made it land. A page that told a clear story, held the detail without overwhelming, and helped a real person make a decision. We want the craft on the surface, the words weighted as heavily as the graphics, and evidence you designed with empathy for people at a moment that mattered. Show the outcome too: the number you moved and the testing that got you there. Applications without a portfolio will not be considered.</p> <p><strong>Experience</strong></p> <p>Typically 5 to 8 years in product design, with a track record of conversion-focused design and A/B testing on acquisition surfaces.<strong><br></strong></p> <p><strong><span class="notion-enable-hover" data-token-index="0">Behaviours &amp; attitude</span></strong></p> <ul> <li><strong><span class="notion-enable-hover" data-token-index="0">Patient-first mindset.</span></strong> You put patient outcomes first. Every decision weighs commercial growth against clinical safety and care, and you don't let one erode the other. You understand real health journeys well enough to make them simple, accessible and worth trusting.</li> <li><strong><span class="notion-enable-hover" data-token-index="0">Collaborative creation.</span></strong> You work well across product, engineering and clinical, and you know a good idea can come from any of them. You listen to feedback and take it on, using it to make the work better.</li> <li><strong><span class="notion-enable-hover" data-token-index="0">Curiosity.</span></strong> You ask why before how. You stay curious about the patient, the problem and the tools you use to solve it, and you're comfortable being a beginner when something new is worth learning.<br>Typically 5 to 8 years in product design, with a track record of conversion-focused design and A/B testing on acquisition surfaces.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Why join Eucalyptus?</strong></h3> <p>Euc is also behind a growing family of digital healthcare clinics (<a href="https://pilot.com.au/">Pilot,</a>&nbsp;<a href="http://www.kinfertility.com.au/">Kin</a>,&nbsp;<a href="http://skin.software/">Software</a>) across men’s health and well-being, fertility, and skincare.</p> <p><strong>Here’s what makes joining Euc unique:</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>What’s next</strong> - Our goal for the next three years is to support <strong>1 million patients globally</strong> to live better for longer. We’re launching into new conditions, demographics, and geographies as we build a truly preventive healthcare ecosystem.</li> <li><strong>Build something world-changing</strong> - We’re on the path to becoming the world’s largest international digital healthcare company. It will be challenging, fast-paced, and deeply rewarding.</li> <li><strong>Make real impact</strong> - You will deliver work that directly shapes patient outcomes and scales evidence-based care across markets.</li> <li><strong>Accelerate your growth</strong> - You will have high ownership, continuous feedback, and dedicated development support.</li> <li><strong>Join a motivated team</strong> - You will collaborate with talented peers to solve complex clinical and operational problems at scale.</li> </ul> <h3>What’s ahead in the UK</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Be an owner</strong> – Your own stake in the business with our employee options program</li> <li><strong>Invest in your growth</strong> – Annual development budget plus 3 days of professional development leave</li> <li><strong>Work flexibly</strong> – Hybrid setup with 3 days a week in our Old Street office, designed for focus and collaboration</li> <li><strong>Support your well-being</strong> – Private health insurance through Vitality or opt for a monthly wellness allowance to spend on what matters most to you</li> <li><strong>Take time off</strong> – 25 days of holiday, enhanced parental leave and work from anywhere 3 weeks out of the year</li> <li><strong>Join a connected team</strong> – A vibrant office culture with regular socials, clubs, after-school sport, and seasonal events</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p><div class="content-conclusion"><p><em>At Eucalyptus, we value individuals from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives, and we embrace the unique qualities each person brings. When you apply, please let us know of any reasonable adjustments you may need during the interview process. We use AI-assisted tools across our business to help our teams work more efficiently, including within our recruitment process. These tools support our team — all hiring decisions are made by real people, and every application is reviewed by a member of our recruitment team.</em></p></div> Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

description: <div class="content-intro"><div id="labeledImage.LOCATION" class="WIFG" data-automation-id="decorationWrapper"> <div class="WNHJ"> <div id="labeledImage.LOCATION--uid38" class="WE-Y WMXY WBAB WF0Y" data-automation-id="responsiveMonikerInput" data-metadata-id="labeledImage.LOCATION" data-uxi-form-item-child-list-index="0"> <div class="WJ-Y"> <p><strong>The <a href="https://www.nytco.com/mission-and-values/" target="_blank"><u>mission</u></a> of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for.&nbsp;</strong></p> </div> </div> </div> </div></div><p><strong>The Audience Manager</strong> is an exciting role within T Brand Studio, the award-winning content studio of The New York Times Advertising department. Inspired by the journalism, creativity and innovation of The New York Times newsroom, the team partners with brands to tell meaningful stories that resonate with our global audience and create lasting impact.</p> <p>Based in London, this role leads the end-to-end management of branded content distribution campaigns across The New York Times' on-site and off-site channels, developing audience strategies and driving campaign optimisation and measurement. Working closely with creative, strategy, sales and media planning teams across London, Paris, Singapore and New York, the Audience Manager helps deliver exceptional campaign performance while contributing to the ongoing evolution of our distribution and measurement capabilities.</p> <p>This is a key client-facing role, partnering directly with agencies and brands to communicate campaign performance, audience insights and business impact. The successful candidate will confidently translate data into compelling stories while building trusted client relationships.</p> <p>The role requires a strong understanding of the evolving media landscape across social, video, audio and editorial formats, alongside a forward-looking mindset that identifies opportunities to enhance our distribution, measurement and optimisation capabilities through new technologies, vendor partnerships and best practices.</p> <p>The role will report directly to the Associate Director of Audience Development &amp; Insights based in London as part of the broader T Brand Strategy Team.&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>Responsibilities</strong></p> <ul> <li>Schedule, manage and optimise distribution campaigns across The New York Times' on-site native placements, social media channels and third-party distribution networks.</li> <li>Develop weekly and end-of-campaign performance reports that translate campaign metrics into actionable insights for clients and internal stakeholders.</li> <li>Advise editorial, production and design teams on branded content best practices, new formats and distribution strategies.</li> <li>Partner with sales, strategy and creative teams during pre-sale to support pitches with audience insights, best practices and performance benchmarks.</li> <li>Manage multiple campaigns simultaneously while collaborating with cross-functional teams across international markets.</li> <li>Research audience behaviour, advertising trends and the competitive landscape to inform campaign strategy and identify new opportunities.</li> <li>Share campaign learnings and best practices to continually improve creative performance.</li> <li>Support the development and delivery of campaign effectiveness and brand measurement solutions, including brand lift studies and attention-based methodologies.</li> <li>Evaluate emerging measurement tools and vendor partnerships to expand T Brand Studio International's measurement capabilities.</li> <li>Collaborate with internal teams and external partners to test and scale new measurement frameworks that demonstrate business outcomes beyond traditional engagement metrics.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Basic Qualifications</strong></p> <ul> <li>Campaign management experience using tools such as Google ads manager, Pressboard, Social Media advertising (Facebook, Instagram, Youtube, Tiktok)&nbsp;</li> <li>Experience with data analysis and storytelling, going beyond the “what” to tell the “why” within research results</li> <li>Experience managing stakeholders in a client facing role</li> <li>Capable of handling multiple projects in a fast paced, deadline driven environment</li> </ul> <p><strong>Preferred Qualifications</strong></p> <ul> <li>Knowledge of media tools, data and audience measurement tools (MRI, Ipsos Affluent Survey, GWI, SimilarWeb or Google Analytics etc.)</li> </ul> <p>REQ-020347</p> <p>#LI-Hybrid</p> <p><span data-sheets-root="1"><span style="text-decoration: underline;"><strong>Additional Compensation and Benefits</strong></span><br><br>For roles in the U.S., dependent on your role, you may be eligible for variable pay, such as an annual bonus and restricted stock. Benefits may include medical, dental and vision benefits, Flexible Spending Accounts (F.S.A.s), a company-matching 401(k) plan, employee stock purchase plan, paid vacation, paid sick days, paid parental leave, tuition reimbursement and professional development programs. <br><br>For roles outside of the U.S., information on benefits will be provided during the interview process.<br><br></span></p><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>Candidate Use of GenAI Tools:</strong></p> <p>We’re excited to learn more about you and your experience. To keep our hiring process as fair and authentic as possible, we ask that you submit your own work and not use GenAI tools to generate substantive content during the application and interview process.</p> <p>If you’re an engineering candidate, we’ll let you know what specific GenAI tools you are permitted to use for your technical assessment.</p> <hr> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p>The New York Times Company is committed to being the world’s best source of independent, reliable and quality journalism. To do so, we embrace a diverse workforce that has a broad range of backgrounds and experiences across our ranks, at all levels of the organization. We encourage people from all backgrounds to apply.</p> <p>We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and do not discriminate on the basis of an individual's sex, age, race, color, creed, national origin, alienage, religion, marital status, pregnancy, sexual orientation or affectional preference, gender identity and expression, disability, genetic trait or predisposition, carrier status, citizenship, veteran or military status and other personal characteristics protected by law. All applications will receive consideration for employment without regard to legally protected characteristics. The U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC)’s Know Your Rights Poster is available&nbsp;<a href="https://www.eeoc.gov/know-your-rights-workplace-discrimination-illegal">here</a>.&nbsp;</p> <p>The New York Times Company will provide reasonable accommodations as required by applicable federal, state, and/or local laws. Individuals seeking an accommodation for the application or interview process should email ----- Emails sent for unrelated issues, such as following up on an application, will not receive a response.</p> <p>For information about The New York Times' privacy practices for job applicants, click <a href="https://nytco-assets.nytimes.com/2020/06/NYT_Applicant_Privacy_Policy.pdf">here</a>.</p> <p>Please beware of fraudulent job postings. The New York Times will not ask job applicants for financial information or for payment, and will not refer you to a third party to do so. You should never send money to anyone who suggests they can provide employment with The New York Times.</p> <p>If you see a fake or fraudulent job posting, or if you suspect you have received a fraudulent offer, you can report it to The New York Times at ----- You can also file a report with the <a href="https://reportfraud.ftc.gov/#/">Federal Trade Commission</a> or your <a href="https://www.naag.org/our-work/center-for-consumer-protection/consumer-file-a-complaint/">state attorney general</a>.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p></div> Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Head of Product and Identity Security
description: <div class="content-intro"><h3><strong>A</strong><strong>BOUT TIDE</strong></h3> <p>At Tide, we help SMEs save time and money in the running of their businesses by not only offering business accounts and related banking services, but also a comprehensive set of highly usable and connected administrative solutions, from invoicing to accounting.</p> <p>Tide is transforming the small business banking market and now supports over 2 million members globally across the UK, India, Germany and France.</p> <p>Using advanced technology, all solutions are designed with SMEs in mind. With quick onboarding, low fees and innovative features, we thrive on making data driven decisions to serve our mission: to help SMEs save time and money so they can get back to doing what they love.</p> <p><strong>Tide facts:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Tide is available for UK, Indian, German and French SMEs</li> <li>Over 2 million members across UK and India</li> <li>Over $300 million raised in funding</li> <li>Over 2,800 Tideans globally</li> <li>Recognised with Great Place to Work certification three years in a row, and among India’s Top 50 Best Workplaces in Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance in 2026</li> <li>We have offices in Central London, with a member support and technology centre in Sofia, Bulgaria, technology centres in Serbia, Romania, Lithuania and Hyderabad and offices in Gurugram, New Delhi, Berlin, Paris and Luxembourg</li> </ul></div><h3>ABOUT THE TEAM:</h3> <p>The Tide Security Engineering team is made up of three core areas: Product Security, Identity, and Threat Detection &amp; Response.</p> <p><strong>Product Security</strong> (this role!) consists of application and cloud security experts. Their mission is to protect the products we build, covering everything from secure design reviews to threat modelling and penetration testing, ensuring security is embedded from the ground up.</p> <p><strong>Identity</strong> (this role!) is responsible for managing Tide's staff identity platform, ensuring that access to systems and infrastructure is secure, seamless, and aligned with modern security practices. The team uses strategies like zero trust, multi-factor authentication, and granular role-based access controls to safeguard our internal operations.</p> <p><strong>Threat Detection &amp; Response</strong> focuses on protecting the company by building a robust detection and automation platform. We're proactive in our defence, constantly hacking ourselves to improve our security posture and staying ahead of emerging threats. Our goal is to make Tide resilient against the ever-evolving threat landscape.</p> <p>While each area has its own focus, collaboration is key - it's why we share the same Slack channel and hold our standups together as one cohesive team, ensuring alignment and seamless communication across all security functions.</p> <p>As the Head of Product and Identity Security, you'll own two of those three areas, reporting directly to the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) and operating as a peer to the Head of Threat Detection &amp; Response. The remit spans application security, penetration testing, cloud security, artificial intelligence (AI) security, secure architecture, identity, and vulnerability operations. You'll lead a global team across the UK, Eastern Europe, and India, and you'll stay close to the technology: this is a player-manager role, where credibility is earned by doing the work as well as directing it. This is a real opportunity to make an impact and have senior influence on the cyber resilience strategy at Tide.</p> <h3><br>ABOUT THE ROLE:&nbsp;</h3> <p><strong>As a Head of Product and Identity Security you will:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Defining the product and identity security strategy in conjunction with the CISO and operationalising it into a funded, sequenced roadmap that the team can execute against.</li> <li>Leading, coaching, and growing a global team across the UK, Eastern Europe, and India; setting clear objectives; running regular 1:1s; and supporting career growth and progression.</li> <li>Owning application security end-to-end, from secure design reviews and threat modelling through to secure coding standards, tooling, and remediation of findings.</li> <li>Running the penetration testing programme across web, mobile and infrastructure, including internal testing and the management of external partners, and staying hands-on where it counts.</li> <li>Owning cloud security posture across our cloud estate, covering configuration, workload protection, detection coverage in partnership with Threat Detection &amp; Response, and the guardrails that keep engineering fast and safe.</li> <li>Setting the approach to AI and agentic security, covering how models, agents and machine learning (ML) pipelines are designed, deployed, monitored and defended, and keeping that approach current as the technology moves.</li> <li>Owning secure architecture so that security requirements are embedded from the ground up in new products, platforms, and integrations rather than retrofitted.</li> <li>Owning Tide's staff identity platform and the wider identity and access management (IAM) roadmap, including zero trust, multi-factor authentication, role-based access control, and joiner, mover, and leaver processes.</li> <li>Standing up and running a rapid-response vulnerability operations capability, with clear service levels for triage and remediation, and tight integration with security operations (SecOps) and engineering.</li> <li>Facing off directly with executives, product leaders, and engineering leadership across the business; articulating risk, trade-offs, and investment cases in language each audience can act on.</li> <li>Delivering the security enablement and security champions programmes so engineering teams can move quickly without security becoming a bottleneck.</li> <li>Acting as a senior escalation point for product and identity security issues, including during high-severity incidents, working alongside Threat Detection &amp; Response.</li> <li>Recruiting and onboarding new team members as the function scales, and building technical capability across the team through mentoring and structured upskilling.</li> <li>Owning performance management for the team, including feedback, development plans, and, where needed, managing underperformance.</li> <li>Defining and reporting the metrics that demonstrate whether the programme is working, including vulnerability ageing and remediation, coverage of secure design reviews, and the reach and effect of enablement activity.</li> </ul> <h3><br>WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR:</h3> <ul> <li>At least ten years of overall experience in cybersecurity, including at least five years in a comparable leadership role, ideally within a technology company or fintech.</li> <li>A background as a hands-on security engineer, ideally including application and/or mobile penetration testing, and the appetite to remain technical as a player-manager.</li> <li>Great knowledge of AI, agentic security, and ML, and a clear point of view on how to secure them in production.</li> <li>A strong grasp of threat modelling, and the ability to articulate risk credibly to both engineering and non-technical audiences.</li> <li>A proven track record of delivering successful security enablement and security champions programmes.</li> <li>Highly organized, with the ability to operationalize a programme and define strategy in conjunction with the CISO.</li> <li>Strong stakeholder management skills and the confidence to face off to executives in the business directly.</li> <li>Experience leading distributed teams across multiple countries and time zones.</li> <li>Excellent spoken and written communication skills.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Nice to have:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience with identity providers (IdPs), privileged access management (PAM), and broader IAM tooling, such as Okta, Ping, and ConductorOne, or equivalents.</li> <li>Experience standing up a rapid-response vulnerability operations or remediation operations function and integrating it with SecOps.</li> </ul> <h3><br>WHAT YOU’LL GET IN RETURN:&nbsp;</h3> <ul> <li>Competitive Compensation - &nbsp;competitive salary and share options</li> <li>Time Off – Generous annual leave on top of bank holidays.</li> <li>Parental Leave – Paid maternity, paternity, and adoption leave to support your family journey.</li> <li>Sabbatical – Extended unpaid and paid leave options after completing milestone years with Tide.</li> <li>Access to salary sacrifice benefits – like Nursery (could save up to 47% on fees!) and Cycle to Work discounts</li> <li>Health Insurance – Comprehensive Private family insurance plan.</li> <li>Life &amp; Accident Cover – Comprehensive accidental and life insurance protection.</li> <li>Mental Wellbeing – Access to therapy sessions, courses, meditations, and workshops.</li> <li>Retirement Planning – Build your retirement fund faster with Tide’s pension scheme on eligible earnings.</li> <li>Volunteering &amp; Development Days – Paid days annually for volunteering or personal growth.</li> <li>Learning &amp; Development – Annual budget for books, courses, coaching, and more.</li> <li>WOO (Work Outside the Office) – Work from abroad for up to 90 days annually.</li> <li>Home Office Setup – Contribution towards setting up your home office</li> <li>Laptop Ownership – Keep your old laptop and get a new one when it’s time for a replacement.</li> <li>Snacks &amp; Meals – Daily breakfast spread with all-day coffee, tea, and juices.</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <h3>TIDEAN WAYS OF WORKING</h3> <p>At Tide, we champion a <strong>flexible workplace </strong>model that<strong> </strong>supports both in-person and remote work to cater to the specific needs of our different teams.&nbsp;</p> <p>While remote work is supported, we believe in the power of face-to-face interactions to foster team spirit and collaboration. Our offices are designed as hubs for innovation and team-building, where we encourage regular in-person gatherings to foster a strong sense of community.</p><div class="content-conclusion"><h3>TIDE IS A PLACE FOR EVERYONE</h3> <p>At Tide, we believe that we can only succeed if we let our differences enrich our culture. Our Tideans come from a variety of backgrounds and experience levels. We consider everyone irrespective of their ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, national origin, veteran, neurodiversity or differently-abled status. We celebrate diversity in our workforce as a cornerstone of our success. Our commitment to a broad spectrum of ideas and backgrounds is what enables us to build products that resonate with our members’ diverse needs and lives.&nbsp;</p> <p>We are One Team and foster a transparent and inclusive environment, where everyone’s voice is heard.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><em>At Tide, we thrive on diversity, embracing various backgrounds and experiences. We welcome all individuals regardless of ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, or disability. title: Regulatory Affairs Associate, Labelling
description: <p><strong>Regulatory Affairs Associate, Labelling</strong></p> <p><strong>Cycle Company:</strong> Cycle Pharmaceuticals Ltd</p> <p><strong>Position Summary:</strong> This is a full-time position within the Regulatory Affairs team working in our Cambridge office on a hybrid basis (minimum 3 days in the office).</p> <p><strong>Salary:&nbsp;</strong>£37,000 to £42,000 depending on experience, plus bonus and benefits<strong>.</strong></p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p>Join our Regulatory Affairs team as a Regulatory Affairs Associate, labelling where you'll have the opportunity to develop your experience in one of the most important parts of our business bringing medicines to patients through clear, accurate and compliant product information.</p> <p>In this role, you’ll support day-to-day labelling activities across Cycle’s product portfolio, helping prepare, review, maintain and update product labelling and artwork for different markets. You’ll work closely with colleagues across Regulatory Affairs, Quality, Medical Affairs, Compliance, Product Development, Supply Chain, Legal and Project Management, as well as external partners.</p> <p>This is a great opportunity for someone early in their regulatory affairs career who enjoys detail, accuracy and coordination, and wants to build specialist expertise in labelling across areas including metabolic, immunology, oncology and neurology.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>Our Company</strong></p> <p>At Cycle, we believe that <strong>Every Single Patient Matters</strong>. This is at the heart of why we work and were looking for people to join our team who share our vision. We know that life-changing treatments need life-improving product support to match, because when you put the two together, great things can happen.</p> <p>Our growing portfolio now covers oncology, haematology, neurology and rare metabolic genetic conditions where we improve existing drugs, repurpose them for new uses and bring generics back to market. Using cutting-edge drug delivery technologies, we enhance the efficiency of treatments, offering patients greater freedom and choice.</p> <p>Headquartered in Cambridge, UK, with a significant US presence, Cycle has scaled rapidly and was named one of the UK’s fastest-growing private companies by The Sunday Times (Sunday Times 100 2024 &amp; Sunday Times 100 Tech 2025). If you want to know more about what we do then, why not check out our website and take a look at some of our patient stories: <a href="https://cyclepharma.com/patient-advocacy/patient-stories/">Patient Stories - Cycle Pharma</a></p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>What you’ll be doing in this role:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Supporting the preparation, review and maintenance of product labelling and artwork, including labels, cartons, leaflets, artwork files and print proofs.</li> <li>Helping to coordinate labelling updates across Cycle’s portfolio, with a particular focus on US requirements with the FDA and relevant UK/MHRA considerations.</li> <li>Reviewing labelling materials for accuracy, consistency and compliance with approved product information and regulatory requirements.</li> <li>Supporting regulatory submissions by preparing, checking and maintaining labelling-related documentation.</li> <li>Managing version control, approval tracking and accurate record keeping for labelling and artwork activities.</li> <li>Working closely with Regulatory Affairs, Quality, Medical Affairs, Compliance, Product Development, Supply Chain, Legal, Project Management and external partners to ensure labelling changes are delivered accurately and on time.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Skills and experience required:</strong></p> <ul> <li>A bachelor’s degree in life sciences or a related subject.</li> <li>At least one year’s experience in Regulatory Affairs, labelling or artwork creation.</li> <li>Some familiarity with regulatory agencies such as the US FDA and MHRA; experience with other non-US regulators would be helpful.</li> <li>Strong attention to detail and the ability to work accurately with regulatory documents and scientific information.</li> <li>Good written and verbal communication skills, with the confidence to work with different teams and external partners.</li> <li>A proactive, organised and reliable approach, with the ability to manage several tasks and meet deadlines.</li> <li>A genuine interest in developing specialist expertise in regulatory labelling.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What can we offer to you:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Competitive salary based on experience.</li> <li>Flexible core working hours of 10am to 4pm and hybrid working.</li> <li>A collaborative, high-performing work environment.</li> <li>Performance-based bonus.</li> <li>Opportunity to join a fast-growing and ambitious business.</li> <li>Company pension scheme.</li> <li>100% employer-paid Private Health Insurance.</li> <li>Life and Critical Illness Insurance.</li> <li>Corporate gym membership.</li> <li>Regular team-building and social events.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Diversity and Inclusion</strong></p> <p><em>At Cycle Pharmaceuticals, we are committed to creating an inclusive, respectful, positive and diverse workplace. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, colour, religion, gender, age, disability, or any other protected characteristic. We actively support and embrace diversity, and we are working to build a team that reflects a wide range of backgrounds and perspectives.</em></p> <p><em>We value your unique contributions and encourage you to join us in shaping a more inclusive future. If you require any reasonable adjustments - whether during the application process or in the workplace - we will be happy to support your needs. At Cycle, equality, inclusion, and respect are at the core of everything we do. We fully comply with all applicable employment laws, including those related to non-discrimination, work authorization, and employment eligibility verification.</em></p> Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

raw.title: Commercial Finance Business Development Manager
raw.description:
About Allica Bank

Allica is the UK’s fastest growing company - and the fastest-growing financial technology (Fintech) firm ever. Our purpose is to help established SMEs, one of the last major underserved opportunities in Fintech.

Established SMEs are the backbone of local communities - representing over a third of our economy - yet have been largely neglected both by traditional high street banks and modern fintech providers.

Kriya sits inside that story as Allica's platform for building new credit products. We already offer invoice finance to mid-market SMEs. We are now evaluating how best to launch unsecured lending products to SMEs, building on the well-known MarketFinance loans franchise, but backed by Allica's balance sheet, cost of funds, and 30,000+ SME customer base.

Role Description
Small businesses can't afford to wait around. When a cash flow gap or a growth opportunity appears, the SMEs we serve need funding that moves at the same speed they do, which is exactly the gap Kriya's unsecured lending products are built to fill.

We are looking for a Commercial Finance BDM to help drive new business across Kriya's unsecured, high-velocity SME lending products. This is an entrepreneurial, high-activity sales role: you'll build and manage your own pipeline of prospects, qualify fast, and take ownership of your numbers. Every conversation with a prospective customer is different, and how well you manage your own pipeline rather than any one big deal is what will make the difference to your results. You will also have Allica’s wider distribution network to make the most of.

The products:

  • Invoice Finance, Export lending, SME loans and working capital products

  • Facility sizes: £100k - £1m

  • Pricing positioned competitively against non-bank competitors

  • Multiple inbound, outbound and referral channels available from day one

  • Room to grow into larger facilities and broader working capital products over time

Principal Accountabilities

  • Build and nurture a high-quality pipeline of SME prospects

  • Run fast, structured qualification conversations to confirm genuine funding need and fit, using your own judgement on which businesses are worth pursuing

  • Own the sales cycle end-to-end: outreach, pitch, objection handling, close

  • Consistently hit and go beyond your weekly and monthly activity and conversion targets

  • Maintain accurate, up-to-date CRM records to support forecasting and pipeline visibility

  • Build repeatable outbound habits: call volume, meeting volume, follow-up cadence

  • Collaborate closely with credit, risk, operations and collections to resolve customer queries quickly and keep deals on track

  • Feed market and competitor intelligence back into the commercial team, and share what's working with the rest of the group

  • Build toward future team growth as origination volume justifies expansion

  • Implement AI in your workflows


Personal Attributes & Experience

  • Experience selling one or more of: SME business loans, working capital loans, merchant cash advance, revenue-based finance, invoice finance, or business lines / cash flow lending.

  • A track record of direct SME new-business sales, not just via the introducer base

  • Demonstrable success operating in short sales cycles with high deal volume, ideally with a proven record of meeting or beating targets

  • Based in London and willing to work 1-2 days a week from the office regularly

  • Background at a high-volume non-bank funder, fintech or embedded lender

  • Exposure to fast, digital-first onboarding and payout journeys

  • A good understanding of the challenges facing small businesses, and the range of finance products SMEs use to manage them

  • Confident, direct communicator, able to explain complex financial products in a simple, compelling way to owners with little experience of commercial finance

  • Resilient and target-driven: you take setbacks in your stride and treat them as feedback

  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy, even when managing a high volume of accounts at pace

  • Organised pipeline management; CRM management, with deals tracked accurately at every stage

  • Comfortable in a hybrid Kriya-inside-Allica setup: startup-pace commercial team, bank-grade governance around it

title: Founding Content Strategist
description: Meet Siena Siena is the Agent of Record for CX, built for consumer brands like Spanx, FIGS, Brooklinen, and Grüns. It runs as a connected multi-agent stack on top of a shared intelligence layer: agents that sell, support, listen, handle social and voice across the entire customer journey, turning every conversation into signal you can act on. The team We are a small, fully distributed, global team. We have built leverage into how we work, which is what lets a team this size move at the speed we do. We hire athletes. Everyone here owns real outcomes, defaults to writing over meetings, communicates with directness, and acts the moment they see something worth acting on. Low ego, high standards, fast clock. If you want to set the bar rather than follow one, keep reading. The Role Siena is shipping faster than the market can absorb, and the words are not keeping up. The market learns about what we build too late, and when it does, the writing doesn't do the product justice. Today launch content is written by the founders and the growth team between everything else, and nobody owns it. With several product launches back to back over the next two quarters and a Founding Creative Director coming in to own the visuals, we need one person who owns every word Siena puts in front of the market: founder-led LinkedIn, the company voice on socials, launches, blog posts, announcements, the scripts behind our videos. You decide what we say, where, and how often, and then you write it. There is no content team underneath you and no copywriters to hand things to. You make the thing. What You'll Do You own all of Siena's content: if it goes out under the Siena name and the market reads it, you wrote it or you signed off on it. You set the strategy for founder-led LinkedIn and the company's own social accounts, write the posts, and own what they do. You ship every product launch with its words ready, announcement, blog, social sequence and founder posts, working with the Creative Director so the words and the visuals land as one thing. You write the scripts for every product video and marketing video, from the launch film to a 30-second product clip, and the Creative Director brings them to screen. You study trends and top performing posts, in our category and outside it, and turn that into a point of view the team can act on, not a swipe file. You know which content moved something, why, and where to double down, and you kill what doesn't work without being asked. You use AI in every part of the work, research, drafting, analysis, distribution, and move faster than a content team would. Your taste is the final filter. Who You Are The Bar: If you're missing any of these, this isn't the role for you. Published writing you can show across blog posts, launch announcements, social, and video scripts. You have shipped content as the only writer at a company or brand, with no team or copywriters behind you. You have worked in eCommerce or marketed to consumer brands and understand how their teams operate. Strong Signal: Not dealbreakers, but what separates a good hire from a great one. You were writing professionally before the current AI tools, and you can tell the difference between a sentence that sounds right and one that's true. You can point to writing that changed what someone did, e.g. the line that got a head of CX to book the demo, the founder post that got forwarded inside a company, the launch that landed. You use AI in every part of your work and none of it reads like AI. You measure your own work and change course on the evidence, not on taste alone. You have run founder-led or executive content before and can show what it did. Nice to Have: Bonus, not required. CX experience in eCommerce, on the brand side or the vendor side. You have marketed AI, automation, or customer experience products. Not a Fit If: You need a content team or copywriters underneath you to produce output. You think content strategy is a calendar. A calendar isn't a point of view. You are anti-AI, or you use AI and ship the first draft. Both are disqualifying. Your best work happens on a slow, protected timeline. Here it's multiple launches in flight and feedback in hours, not weeks. Why Siena? Real ownership. You will own problems, not tasks, with the autonomy to solve them your way and the trust to do it without a manager in your inbox. Work that ships and matters. What you build reaches real consumer brands fast. A category we are creating. The Agent of Record is new ground, with unsolved problems and cutting-edge models, not a crowded field to compete in. A team that respects your judgment. Globally distributed, async-first, low bureaucracy. We hire adults and treat you like one. Great salary plus equity or stock grants. Own a piece of what you build. Learning budget. If you are growing, so are we. AI-fluency by default. Few places will push your work with production AI further or faster. Our values The people who thrive here are curious, customer-obsessed, and take ownership without being asked. They fix problems first and explain later. They're direct about feedback - both giving and receiving it - because they care more about getting things right than being polite. They maintain high standards while moving at startup speed, and they build real relationships with teammates because they know that's how great work gets done. When things get tough, they adapt and keep pushing forward. Our approach to AI The people who thrive here treat AI like a natural extension of themselves. They've built their own ecosystem of agents - some for research, others for debugging, writing, analysis, or writing code. They know which AI works best for what problem.
